title: Batchsmith heuristic weaver: workload profiling and continuous batch param synthesis
creator: Alma Reyes
description:
Goal: Build a resilient recommendation engine (Batchsmith) that proposes continuous batching and KV cache parameters per workload cohort, produces conservative safe-applies, and provides automated rollback instrumentation. This ticket covers the first implementation of the heuristics synthesizer, profiling pipeline, and the staged apply/rollback playbook used for canary -> graduated rollout.

Scope:
- Workload signature collector: lightweight per-route sampler (latency, seq_length, KV-hit-ratio, request coalescence potential).
- Heuristics synthesizer: map signatures to parameter deltas (batch_size_target, max_concurrent_sequences, kv_prefix_cache_ttl, coalescing_window_ms) with cost/latency tradeoff scoring.
- Safety guardrail engine: conservative thresholds, MAPE-based prediction bands, and rollback triggers (latency P90 increase, error-rate delta, token-cost-per-request regression).
- Continuous applier: staged canaries, shadow apply telemetry, automatic rollback and manual override hooks.

Out of scope for this ticket: UI surfaced recommendations (Console work is separate), deep RL-based tuning, and multi-tenant cross-correlation analysis (follow-up phase).
acceptance_criteria:
- Batchsmith can ingest sampled workload signatures for 10 test routes and produce parameter suggestions that save >=10% token-cost in synthetic replay without exceeding 95% baseline latency P90.
- A staged canary apply flow runs end-to-end: shadow apply -> 5% traffic canary -> 25% -> 100%, with automatic rollback on configured SLO breach.
- Telemetry emitted: batchsmith.suggestion.v1 (route, signature_hash, params, score), batchsmith.apply.event (canary_id, stage, delta_metrics), and batchsmith.rollback.event (reason, prior_params).
- Documentation: runbook describing manual abort, rollback steps, and tuning knobs available to SREs and PMs.
- Security review completed and KMS key usage for any config artifacts that may contain customer identifiers.
notes:
Design trade-offs considered:
- Conservative defaults vs aggressive cost-first suggestions: we choose conservative defaults for first 3 quarters of rollout to avoid customer impact and gather signal.
- Sampling budget: heavy sampling increases accuracy but costs tokens and compute; implement an adaptive sampler that increases sampling only for high-variance routes.
- KV vs batching tension: some workloads benefit more from KV TTL tuning than batch size; heuristics synthesizer will compute an estimated marginal ROI per parameter to avoid simultaneous conflicting changes.

Technical approach summary:
1) Lightweight profiler runs in sidecar mode producing 1-min aggregated signatures to centralized ingestion (max 2% added latency and bounded memory).
2) Offline synthesizer runs nightly producing candidate parameter sets and an expected delta-cost/delta-latency vector via synthetic replay.
3) Online safety controller performs shadow applies (no effect on real KV/batcher) to validate predictions under live traffic before canary.
4) Apply orchestration uses incremental traffic splits, monotonic checks, and a pre-flight checklist evaluated by the safety controller.

Key metrics to monitor: cost-per-1k-requests, P50/P90 latency, error-rate, KV hit-rate, suggestion acceptance rate.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (shadow validation, week 1): collect signatures, run offline synth on test cluster (internal), validate predictions with shadow apply.
Phase 1 (canary, week 2-3): 5% traffic canary for 24h -> if stable 25% for 48h -> 100% slow roll over 48h segments. Automated rollback triggers set to: P90 latency +15% over baseline for >15 minutes OR error-rate absolute +0.5% increase.
Phase 2 (graduated): expand to non-critical customers and expose opt-in toggle in Console.
Fallback: on rollback, reapply prior safe params and blacklist offending signature hash from further auto-applies until manual review.
rollback_strategy:
- Immediate auto-rollback when safety controller detects threshold breach (emit batchsmith.rollback.event).
- If auto-rollback fails or is noisy, safety controller pins route to 'manual review' state and notifies on-call SRE with runbook link.
- Maintain immutable audit of applied params (who/what/when) in secure config store to allow quick reversion.
- For cascading failures, have global kill-switch to revert Batchsmith applier across all routes.
telemetry_and_alerting:
Events: batchsmith.suggestion.v1, batchsmith.shadow.validate, batchsmith.apply.stage, batchsmith.rollback.event.
Dashboards: per-route suggestion heatmap, predicted_vs_actual_cost scatter, canary-stage metrics.
Alerts: CanarySLOBreached (on-call), SuggestionRegressionSpike (>20% mismatch between predicted and actual).
Logs: structured JSON with signature_hash, cohort_id, candidate_params, and simulation_metrics.
Retention: 90 days for suggestion events, 365 days for apply/rollback audit.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for heuristics transforms and ROI computation.
- Integration tests: synthetic replay harness that runs the candidate params against recorded traces and validates latency/cost deltas.
- Chaos test: introduce transient latency spikes in staging to validate rollback triggers.
- Load test: 10k RPS replay across 50 synthetic routes to ensure applier scale.
security_considerations:
- All signature hashes must be irreversible (HMAC with per-customer salt stored in KMS) to avoid storing PII.
- Config artifacts stored encrypted in vault with KMS key access limited to SRE/Product-Owner roles.
- Review required for any endpoint that can change live batcher/kv parameters.
risks:
- False positives: heuristics might suggest params that regress tail latency for long-tail sequences. Mitigation: conservative scoring and shadow validation.
- Telemetry gaps: insufficient sampling will produce noisy predictions. Mitigation: adaptive sampler and manual override.
- Operational complexity: rollout management increases SRE surface area; mitigate with clear runbooks and automation to revert.
